summary: Join our Source Water Protection and Conservation Training Course to gain essential knowledge and skills for preserving water quality and sustainability.
lede: Keeping drinking-water sources safe means identifying threats across a catchment and choosing practical ways to reduce them. The course is for water, environmental, conservation, and WASH professionals who need to manage upstream risks and coordinate protection efforts. Participants practise mapping and prioritizing threats, developing protection plans, selecting interventions, and setting up monitoring and reporting to track progress.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for a wide range of professionals who are directly involved in protecting drinking-water sources and managing upstream ecosystems.
audience: Water utility managers, NRW teams, and catchment
Public sector staff in water, environment, health
NGO WASH, climate resilience, and conservation program
Community-based organizations and local water user associations
Donor-funded project officers and M&E teams
modules: Foundations of Source Water Protection and Conservation
Understanding Catchments and Source Water Systems
Source Water Risk Mapping and Data Collection
Designing a Practical Source Water Protection Plan (SWPP)
Protection and Conservation Interventions That Work
Financing, Budgeting, and Value-for-Money for Protection
prerequisites: Participants should have a basic understanding of environmental science and water management principles. Familiarity with GIS, stakeholder engagement, and regulatory frameworks is beneficial but not required.
topics: Water & wastewater treatment and utility management
